ir2_revolution.topic: 1979 revolution: break with Israel, mission to PLO, Khomeini's positions, Quds Day

claims.text: Israel's mission in Tehran was a de facto representation opened 6 March 1950, never a formally recognised embassy; its last head was Yossef Harmelin (1978-79); staff left on 18 February 1979 (infobox gives 17 Feb).

On 19 February 1979 Arafat's delegation was symbolically handed the keys of the former Israeli mission; NYT 19 Feb 1979: 'The sacked Israeli mission here has been donated to the Palestinian movement'; the street (Kakh) was renamed Palestine Street; the building became the Palestinian embassy.

Arafat arrived in Tehran 17 February 1979, two weeks after Khomeini's return; Iran severed ties with Israel during the visit; the mission became the PLO embassy headed by Hani al-Hassan; a militant close to Abu Jihad said Khomeini told Arafat 'there is no Palestinian cause; it is an Islamic cause'; Arafat later sided with Iraq in the war.
Khomeini was arrested in 1963 after denouncing the Shah and Israel; a manifesto he and eight senior scholars signed accused the Shah of submission to the US and Israel.

On 7 August 1979 Khomeini called on Muslims to 'consecrate the last Friday of the holy month of Ramadan as Al-Quds Day'; the Iranian government organises the marches, at which crowds chant 'Death to Israel' and 'Death to America'; the BBC judged it never took root among Muslims at large.
After the revolution hundreds were laid off in Israel's defence industries; Israel-Iran trade had been about $200m a year in the Shah's last years (Klieman 1985).

ir2_arms.topic: Israeli arms to Iran 1980-1988 and Iran-Contra

claims.text: Iran-Iraq war: 22 September 1980 to 20 August 1988; estimates exceed 1,000,000 deaths, Iran suffering more; total casualties estimated at one to two million.

First Israeli sale: F-4 Phantom tyres in early 1980; 250 tyres flown 24 October 1980 (Gwertzman, NYT, 22 Aug 1981); Brzezinski wrote 'we learned, much to our dismay' Israelis were secretly supplying spare parts.
IranWire: in early 1980 Begin 'confirmed the shipment of tyres for Phantom fighter jets'; in exchange Khomeini 'permitted many Iranian Jews to emigrate'.

Operation Seashell (1981): about $75m of arms from Israeli stocks incl. 150 M-40 antitank guns and 24,000 shells; flown by Transporte Aereo Rioplatense charters until the July 1981 crash (Armenia), then by ship (Bergman 2008).

Estimates of total sales: Jaffee Center ~$500m 1981-83 (via Parsi); other arms experts >$500m a year (Marshall/Scott/Hunter); internal US reports approaching $2bn a year (Hersh, NYT 8 Dec 1991); Israeli press $50-100m over several years; arms dealer Ahmad Haidari ~80% of weaponry bought after war began from Israel (Parsi).
NYT reported March 1982: $100-200m in arms and ammunition delivered from Western Europe to Iran in past 18 months, Israel possibly involved in nearly half.

Sharon May 1982 in US 'deliberately confirmed' small Israeli shipments to clear Israel of 'the smear of being Iran's major arms supplier'; said 'No America-made equipment was involved and quantities shipped were very small'.

Sharon to Washington Post May 1982: 'Iraq is Israel's enemy and we hope that diplomatic relations between us and Iran will be renewed as in the past'; four months later in Paris: 'Israel has a vital interest in the continuing of the war in the Persian Gulf, and in Iran's victory' (as quoted by Marshall, Scott, Hunter).
Beit-Hallahmi dates a Sharon Paris press conference saying sales had US consent to 28 September 1983.

Moshe Arens, ambassador, told Boston Globe in 1982 Israel shipped US spare parts to Iran coordinated with US government 'at almost the highest levels'; WaPo reported Haig approved Israeli shipments in 1981; Haig denied.
Dec 1991 report: Reagan administration in 1981 secretly allowed Israel to sell 'several billion dollars' worth' of US-made arms to Iran (officials say).
Israel's reasons per CSM: keep Iraq ('archenemy') tied up, intelligence ties with Iranian officials, foreign exchange; Israel sought US approval to ship surplus US arms despite the embargo.
Senior Israeli officials cited three reasons for 1985 shipments: Iraq gaining upper hand, appearing useful to US, protecting Iran's Jewish community.

Bergman: three goals - restore influence lost with Shah, prevent Iraqi conquest of Iran, business for arms industry. Khomeini denied receiving Israeli arms in 24 Aug 1981 speech, calling it 'childish nonsense' (Parsi).

Iran bombed Osirak in September 1980 (Scorch Sword) and did not acknowledge it in war records; IranWire: 'no credible evidence of direct collaboration' in Israel's June 1981 strike; RAND 2011 says Israel received Iranian intelligence.
US satellite intelligence to Iraq from 1987; US knew of Iraqi chemical use from 1983; Reagan margin note 'An Iranian victory is unacceptable' (per Francona).
Peres's 1984 government stopped arms supplies to Iran under US pressure; Peres stressed in Nov 1986 that Israel acted to help free US hostages; officials said the war 'ties down Iraq'.

Kimche met McFarlane 3 July 1985; 20 Aug 1985 first 96 TOWs Israel to Iran, no hostage released; Reagan approved ~100 TOWs with US replacement of Israeli stocks; second shipment of 408 TOWs; Weir released 15 Sept.

Walsh: Israel shipped 504 US-made TOWs to Iran in Aug-Sept 1985 'With U.S. acquiescence'; Weir 'was released as a result'; 18 HAWKs flown from Israel to Iran on CIA proprietary ~25 Nov 1985 after El Al plan for 80 aborted.

Iranica: Peres first suggested contacts; Nir, Schwimmer, Nimrodi; seven shipments Aug 1985-Nov 1986: 2,004 TOWs, 18 HAWKs, 200+ HAWK spare parts; three hostages freed; Iran returned HAWKs; Israeli markings; Feb 1986 ~1,000 TOWs under US direction; prices $6,000/$10,000/$12,000; diversion of Feb 1986 residuals to Contras.

CSM 1987 chronology: Kimche in July 1985 said arms 'probably will be a condition'; Weir released 14 Sept 1985; Jan 17 1986 finding; Ash-Shiraa 3 Nov 1986; 20 Nov 1986 report that Israel with US approval shipped 2,008 TOWs and 235 Hawks.
Nov 1985 HAWK shipment returned by Iran after it found obsolete arms; US took over operation.
Rafsanjani on 4 Nov 1986 confirmed US shipments; later told Hamshahri Israeli HAWKs 'had to be returned'; Iran paid $14m of $22m deal.
Ledeen met Peres 3 May 1985; North 4-6 Dec 1985 proposed direct sales and told Israeli officials profits would help Contras; shipments 17 Feb 1986 500 TOWs, May 508, 28 Oct 500.
Bush pardoned Weinberger, Abrams, Clarridge, Fiers, George, McFarlane on 24 December 1992.

Audit re-check: Walsh ch.18: 'With U.S. acquiescence, Israel shipped 504 U.S.-made TOW missiles to Iran in August and September of 1985'; Weir 'was released as a result'; El Al 747 plan for 80 HAWKs; a CIA proprietary carried 18 HAWKs, leaving Israel late 24 November and arriving early 25 November 1985

Audit re-check: Iranica: Peres first suggested contacts; 2,004 TOWs, 18 HAWKs, over 200 HAWK spare parts in seven shipments Aug 1985-Nov 1986; three hostages freed (Weir, Jenco, Jacobsen); Iran test-fired one HAWK and returned the rest, lacking high-altitude capability and bearing Israeli markings; $6,000/$10,000/$12,000 per TOW

Audit re-check: Brzezinski 1986: 'Some Israeli like [Kimche] may have taken the initial steps' and 'there may have been a strong temptation on the US side to move in that direction as well'; Shamir rejected US charges Israel helped channel money to the Contras

Audit re-check: Israel's official line cast it as a 'willing helper'; officials did not dispute reports Israel conceived the plan; Peres said Israel was motivated by helping free hostages; Iran 'sitting astride the Persian Gulf'

Audit re-check: a May 1985 CIA paper proposed 'easing' the arms embargo to reach 'moderate' Iranian factions; William Buckley, CIA Beirut station chief, held by Islamic Jihad; McFarlane said Reagan gave verbal approval by mid-1985; Reagan and Meese said he was unaware before the 17 January 1986 finding
Audit re-check: Bergman (via HNN): had Khomeini taken power later 'he might have taken over a country [equipped] with long-range missiles capable of carrying nuclear warheads'
Audit re-check: Proclamation 6518 pardons Abrams, Clarridge, Fiers, George, McFarlane and Weinberger: 'I am doing what I believe honor, decency, and fairness require'
